# 1 Kings Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-Solomon made-himself-a-son-in-law with Pharaoh king-of Egypt, and-took ʾet-the-daughter-of Pharaoh, and-brought-her to the-City-of David, until he-finished building ʾet-his-house and-ʾet-the-house-of YHWH and-ʾet-the-wall-of Jerusalem all-around.

**2** Only, the-people were-sacrificing on-the-high-places, for a-house had-not-been-built for-the-name-of YHWH until those days.

**3** And-Solomon loved ʾet-YHWH, walking in-the-statutes-of David his-father; only, on-the-high-places he was-sacrificing and-burning-incense.

**4** And-the-king went to-Gibeon to-sacrifice there, for it was the-great high-place. A-thousand burnt-offerings Solomon offered upon that altar.

**5** In-Gibeon YHWH appeared to-Solomon in-a-dream-of the-night. And-God said, "Ask — what shall-I-give to-you?"

**6** And-Solomon said, "You have-done with your-servant David my-father great ḥesed, as he-walked before-you in-faithfulness and-in-righteousness and-in-uprightness-of heart with-you. And-you-kept for-him ʾet-this great ḥesed, and-you-gave to-him a-son sitting upon his-throne, as-this day.

**7** And-now, YHWH my-God, you have-made-king ʾet-your-servant in-place-of David my-father. And-I am a-small youth; I-do-not know going-out or-coming-in.

**8** And-your-servant is in-the-midst-of your-people whom you-chose, a-great people that cannot be-numbered or-counted from-multitude.

**9** And-give to-your-servant a-hearing heart to-judge ʾet-your-people, to-understand between good and-evil. For who is-able to-judge ʾet-this your-weighty people?"

**10** And-the-word was-good in-the-eyes-of the-Lord, that Solomon asked ʾet-this thing.

**11** And-God said to-him, "Because you-asked ʾet-this thing, and-you-did-not ask for-yourself many days, and-you-did-not ask for-yourself riches, and-you-did-not ask the-life-of your-enemies, but-you-asked for-yourself understanding to-hear judgment —

**12** behold, I-have-done according-to-your-words. Behold, I-have-given to-you a-wise and-understanding heart, so-that like-you there-has-not-been before-you, and-after-you there-shall-not arise like-you.

**13** And-also what you-did-not ask I-have-given to-you, both riches and-honor, so-that there-shall-not-be a-man like-you among-the-kings all your-days.

**14** And-if you-walk in-my-ways, keeping my-statutes and-my-commandments, as David your-father walked, then-I-will-lengthen ʾet-your-days."

**15** And-Solomon awoke, and-behold — a-dream. And-he-came to-Jerusalem and-stood before the-ark-of the-covenant-of the-Lord, and-offered-up burnt-offerings and-made peace-offerings, and-made a-feast for-all his-servants.

**16** Then two women, prostitutes, came to the-king, and-stood before-him.

**17** And-the-one woman said, "Please, my-lord, I and-this woman dwell in-one house, and-I-gave-birth with-her in-the-house.

**18** And-it-was on-the-third day after-my-giving-birth, and-this woman also gave-birth. And-we were together; there-was-no stranger with-us in-the-house — only the-two-of-us in-the-house.

**19** And-the-son-of this woman died in-the-night, because she-lay upon-him.

**20** And-she-arose in-the-middle-of the-night and-took ʾet-my-son from-beside-me — and-your-maidservant was-asleep — and-laid-him in-her-bosom, and-ʾet-her-dead son she-laid in-my-bosom.

**21** And-I-arose in-the-morning to-nurse ʾet-my-son, and-behold — dead. And-I-looked-at-him in-the-morning, and-behold — it-was-not my-son whom I-bore."

**22** And-the-other woman said, "No! For my-son is the-living and-your-son is the-dead." And-this-one said, "No! For your-son is the-dead and-my-son is the-living." And-they-spoke before the-king.

**23** And-the-king said, "This-one says, 'This is my-son, the-living, and-your-son is the-dead,' and-this-one says, 'No! For your-son is the-dead and-my-son is the-living.'"

**24** And-the-king said, "Bring to-me a-sword." And-they-brought the-sword before the-king.

**25** And-the-king said, "Divide ʾet-the-living child in-two, and-give the-half to-the-one and-the-half to-the-other."

**26** And-the-woman whose-son was the-living said to the-king — for her-compassion burned over her-son — and-she-said, "Please, my-lord, give to-her ʾet-the-living newborn, and-dying do-not kill-him." But-the-other said, "Neither mine nor-yours shall-he-be — divide!"

**27** And-the-king answered and-said, "Give to-her ʾet-the-living newborn, and-dying do-not kill-him. She is his-mother."

**28** And-all Israel heard ʾet-the-judgment that the-king had-judged, and-they-feared before the-king, for they-saw that the-wisdom-of God was in-him to-do justice.

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **3:1 — "made-himself-a-son-in-law with Pharaoh"**: Hebrew va-yitḥaten — a reflexive verb emphasizing the political nature of marriage alliance. Solomon initiates the relationship.

2. **3:9 — "a-hearing heart" (לֵב שֹׁמֵעַ)**: Not "wisdom" but literally a heart that can hear/listen. Solomon asks for judicial discernment, not abstract intelligence.

3. **3:9 — "your-weighty people" (כָּבֵד)**: The Hebrew kavod root — the people are "heavy," meaning numerous, significant, and difficult to govern.

4. **3:15 — "and-behold — a-dream"**: The Hebrew syntax (ve-hinneh ḥalom) expresses Solomon's moment of realization — the encounter with God was real, yet accessed through a dream.

5. **3:26 — "her-compassion burned" (נִכְמְרוּ רַחֲמֶיהָ)**: The verb kamar means to grow hot, to be stirred deeply. Raḥamim (compassion) shares its root with reḥem (womb) — this is visceral, maternal love.

— EMET
